Subject: Tax Assistant API Webhook Instructions

taxes, filing, deductions, income, forms, W-2, 1099, standard deduction, itemize, home office, married filing jointly, tax bracket, refund, IRS.

  "instruction": "Whenever the user asks for tax advice, filing guid

User: I want to file my 2024 taxes correctly. I'm single in Austin TX. W-2 from Coastal Manufacturing: $68,200. Additional income: $16,300 (photography, 3 clients), $2,100 from Capital One 360, $420 from Merrill Edge. Home office: 120 sq ft exclusive; I pay $1,750/month for 740 sq ft. Deductions: $5,100 student loan interest (Nelnet, 2018–2021); $1,500 to Salvation Army have receipt; $1,050 unreimbursed expenses. Can you tell me what I can deduct, whether to itemize or take the standard deduction, how to tr

eat the home office, and what forms I need?
Assistant: Here’s how your 2024 federal return should shake out based on what you shared (single, TX):

What you can deduct
- Standard vs itemized
  - 2024 standard deduction (single): $14,600.
  - Your itemizable amounts listed: $1,500 charitable. With no mortgage interest or SALT taxes provided, itemizing won’t beat $14,600. You should take the standard deduction.

- Student loan interest (Nelnet)
  - Deductible up to $2,500 if paid in 2024 on qualified loans an

d you’re not a dependent.
  - Phaseout for singles in 2024: MAGI roughly $80,000–$95,000. With your income mix, you’ll likely be in the phaseout, so you probably won’t get the full $2,500—expect a reduced amount (ballpark $1,800–$2,300 depending on final MAGI). The exact number finalizes after business profit, half SE tax deduction, etc.

- Home office (photography business)
  - Space: 120 sq ft exclusive use; home is 740 sq ft → business-use % ≈ 16.2%.
  - Methods:
    - Actual-expense method (likely best

for you as a renter):
      - Rent: $1,750 × 12 = $21,000 × 16.2% ≈ $3,405 deductible on Schedule C.
      - You can also include the same % of utilities/renter’s insurance if applicable.
      - Internet/cell are separate Schedule C expenses based on business-use %, not via home office percentage.
    - Simplified method: $5 × 120 sq ft = $600 (no Form 8829, no actuals).
  - Choose one method; you can switch year to year.

- Unreimbursed expenses ($1,050)
  - If these are W‑2 employee job expenses: not ded

uctible for 2024 (suspended through 2025).
  - If they’re ordinary/necessary for your photography work: fully deductible on Schedule C (reduce SE income).

- Qualified Business Income (QBI)
  - If Schedule C shows a net profit, you’ll likely get a QBI deduction up to 20% of that profit (Form 8995), subject to taxable-income limits. This is in addition to the standard deduction and half of SE tax deduction.

How your income is treated
- W‑2 wages: $68,200 reported on Form 1040.
- Photography income: $16,300

gross on Schedule C, minus business expenses (home office and any other business costs). Net profit is subject to both income tax and self-employment (SE) tax. Expect SE tax of about 15.3% on roughly 92.35% of your net profit; half of the SE tax is an above‑the‑line deduction on Schedule 1.
- Bank interest: $2,100 from Capital One 360 is taxable interest (1099‑INT). Because interest > $1,500, you’ll file Schedule B.
- Merrill Edge $420: report per the 1099 (interest, dividends, and/or capital gains). It’s t

axable and may also appear on Schedule B (dividends) and/or Schedule D/8949 (capital gains), depending on what it is.

Forms you’ll likely need
- Form 1040
- Schedule 1 (business income from Schedule C; student loan interest deduction; half SE tax deduction)
- Schedule C (photography income/expenses)
- Schedule SE (self-employment tax)
- Form 8829 (home office) if you use the actual-expense method; not needed for the simplified method
- Schedule B (interest > $1,500; include any dividends too)
- Schedule D

and Form 8949 if your Merrill Edge amount includes capital gains
- Form 8995 (QBI deduction)
- Schedule A only if you decide to itemize (likely not)
- Form 8283 only if your $1,500 Salvation Army gift was noncash property and total noncash gifts exceed $500 (not needed for cash donations)

Quick estimates based on what you provided
- Home office (actual): about $3,405 deductible on Schedule C (rent only; add utilities/insurance if applicable).
- Student loan interest: capped at $2,500 and likely partially p

hased out given your income; you’ll get the exact figure once AGI is finalized.
- Charitable: $1,500 only helps if itemizing—likely you won’t.

Open questions to finalize
- Is the $1,050 in unreimbursed expenses for your photography business (so we put it on Schedule C), or for your W‑2 job (not deductible)?
- What exactly is the $420 from Merrill Edge (interest, dividends, or realized gains)?
- Any additional business expenses (equipment, supplies, software, mileage, internet/cell business use, insurance)

we should include on Schedule C?
- Was the Salvation Army donation cash or goods?

If you want, share those details and I’ll firm up the deductions and give you a tighter tax estimate.
